description: A single-panel figure consisting of a two-row table rendered as an image (no curves, micrographs or schematics). The table has three columns headed exactly: "Temperature", "γ_SFE/mJ·m⁻²" (stacking fault energy, in mJ·m⁻²) and "ΔG^{γ→ε}/J·mol⁻¹" (the Gibbs free-energy difference for the γ→ε martensitic transformation, in J·mol⁻¹). Its two data rows are condition labels, not numbers: "RT" (room temperature) and "LNT" (liquid nitrogen temperature). The values printed are: RT → γ_SFE = 62.64 mJ·m⁻² and ΔG^{γ→ε} = 804.22 J·mol⁻¹; LNT → γ_SFE = 49.46 mJ·m⁻² and ΔG^{γ→ε} = 576.90 J·mol⁻¹. The table therefore shows that cooling from RT to LNT lowers both the stacking fault energy (62.64 → 49.46 mJ·m⁻², a decrease of about 13.2 mJ·m⁻²) and the γ→ε driving-force parameter (804.22 → 576.90 J·mol⁻¹). The caption identifies the tabulated quantities as "γ and ΔG^{γ→ε} at RT and LNT"; note that the caption's second column header is typeset as "ΔG^{z→ε}", which the image renders as "ΔG^{γ→ε}" — most plausibly the same quantity with the γ glyph mis-transcribed. There are no error bars, no axis labels and no other graphical elements; the table is the entire figure.

observations.observation: The figure is a table image with column headers 'Temperature', 'γ_SFE/mJ·m⁻²' and 'ΔG^{γ→ε}/J·mol⁻¹'.
Row 'RT' lists γ_SFE = 62.64 mJ·m⁻² and ΔG^{γ→ε} = 804.22 J·mol⁻¹.
Row 'LNT' lists γ_SFE = 49.46 mJ·m⁻² and ΔG^{γ→ε} = 576.90 J·mol⁻¹.
The stacking fault energy of the γ phase is lower at LNT (49.46 mJ·m⁻²) than at RT (62.64 mJ·m⁻²), a decrease of about 13 mJ·m⁻².
ΔG^{γ→ε} decreases from 804.22 J·mol⁻¹ at RT to 576.90 J·mol⁻¹ at LNT.
Only two temperature conditions are tabulated, labelled RT and LNT; no intermediate temperatures are given.
The table contains no error bars or uncertainty values; each entry is a single number.
The caption states the figure presents 'γ and ΔG^{γ→ε} at RT and LNT'.

In the caption the free-energy column header is typeset as 'ΔG^{z→ε}/J·mol⁻¹', whereas the image renders it as 'ΔG^{γ→ε}/J·mol⁻¹'; the two readings are reported as printed and appear to denote the same γ→ε quantity.
The paper abstract reports yield strength, tensile strength and total elongation of 251 MPa, 580 MPa and 52 % at RT, increasing to 497 MPa, 945 MPa and 75.5 % at LNT for the Fe35Mn6Al0.1C steel.
The paper title attributes the property improvement to an 'underlined deformation twinning mechanism', which this table is used to support via the lowered SFE at LNT.
